amendments.because: Listing every test in the new fix's Done-when duplicates next's lines and grows without limit; the fix names the failed run instead
amendments.done_when: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command for them

done_when: When the latest scheduled run of a workflow failed, forge next names its failed jobs and every failing test, and gives one forge fix start command for that failed run (or the started fix's next step)

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. `_failed_schedules` keys alerts by a cleaned workflow name. Distinct workflow names such as `Build & Test` and `Build Test` both become `Build Test`, so when both latest scheduled runs fail, the second overwrites the first. `forge next` then omits one run’s failed jobs, tests and fix command. The named proof covers identical names distinguished by file path, but not names that collide after cleaning.
findings.title: Not done: When the latest scheduled run of a workflow failed, forge next names its failed jobs and every failing test, and gives one forge f

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Scale. After the one-minute cache expires, this loop starts a separate `gh run list` process and network request for every active workflow, including workflows with no schedule. A client repo with 40 workflows makes at least 41 sequential GitHub CLI calls whenever `forge next` refreshes; the context and handoff hooks also use this report. That adds substantial delay to a routine command. [GitHub CLI documents that workflow listing includes active workflows by default](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_workflow_list).
findings.title: Checking every workflow serially slows forge next in larger repos

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 3, Harm 2
The parser recognizes only pytest-style `FAILED` or `ERROR` lines containing `::`. Scheduled Vitest and Go jobs can fail with named tests but no matching line, so `forge next` names the job without its failing tests. The shipped guidance supports these runners. [Vitest’s reporter format](https://vitest.dev/guide/reporters) and [Go’s failing-test example](https://go.dev/doc/tutorial/add-a-test) show different output. This additional language case is outside the named Done-when case.
findings.title: Follow-up: name JavaScript and Go test failures in scheduled runs

why: A failing nightly full run on macOS or Windows is easy to miss, and Windows stayed red for days unseen
